chapter.title: Reflection and Symmetry
chapter.tagline: Crafting birthday cutouts, folding paper along lines of symmetry, and mirror reflections
chapter.overview: Prem and Manu prepare 'Happy Birthday' cutouts for Lali's birthday. They recall lines of symmetry from Grade 4 to fold paper and cut symmetrical letters like 'A', 'M', and 'T' in a single snip. They explore mirror reflection symmetries and mask making.

sections.title: Birthday Cutouts: Lines of Symmetry
sections.subtitle: Cutting symmetrical letters by folding paper in half

storyNarrative.dialogue: Manu, don't cut the whole letter 'A' freehand! Fold the paper down the middle—the letter 'A' is symmetrical, so we only need to draw and cut half of it!

concept.heading: Line (Reflectional) Symmetry
concept.keyRule: A figure has reflectional symmetry if a line can divide it into two identical halves that coincide exactly when folded.

questions.prompt: Which of these capital letters has a vertical line of symmetry?
questions.hint: Folding 'M' along a vertical crease matches left and right halves perfectly.

sections.title: Horizontal vs. Vertical Lines of Symmetry
sections.subtitle: Discovering letters with one, two, or no lines of symmetry

storyNarrative.dialogue: Look at the letter 'H'! It has BOTH a vertical line of symmetry and a horizontal line of symmetry!

concept.heading: Multiple Lines of Symmetry
concept.keyRule: Letters like 'H', 'I', 'O', and 'X' possess both horizontal and vertical axes of symmetry.

sections.title: Mirror Reflections & Symmetrical Patterns
sections.subtitle: Checking symmetry with a pocket mirror along the mirror line

storyNarrative.dialogue: Place your pocket mirror on the dashed line. The reflection completes the other half as if by magic!

concept.heading: Mirror Reflection Invariance
concept.keyRule: An object and its reflection across a mirror line are congruent and equidistant from the mirror axis.

options: The mirror reflection recreates the complete heart
